title: Customer Care Guide: Controllable Disruptions and the Reinstatement Fee — Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
**Compensation term.** The reinstatement-fee disruption rate on a credit of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers counts the disruption records with a controllable cause recorded on the customer's tickets under Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand in the last 12 calendar months. The rate is:

- **0.75** for at least 2 such records;
- **0.90** for exactly one;
- **1** for none.

**Window.** A reinstatement-fee window of the last so many calendar months holds the entries dated fewer than that many whole calendar months before the date the reinstatement fee is worked out, so it rolls back from that date and is not a count of completed calendar months.

**Which records count.** Disruption records on any of the customer's tickets whose cause is classified controllable, recorded inside the window. Records with an uncontrollable cause do not count.

## Count and rate

| Controllable-cause disruption records in the last 12 calendar months | Disruption rate |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 0.75 |
| exactly 1 | 0.90 |
| none | 1 |

## Hypothetical case (fee worked out on 20 May 2026)

The customer's tickets carry a controllable delay record dated 5 February 2026, an uncontrollable cancellation record dated 1 March 2026, and a controllable cancellation record dated 20 May 2025. The 20 May 2025 record lies 12 whole calendar months back and falls outside the window. The uncontrollable record does not count. One record counts, so the rate is 0.90.
